newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian stocks end higher, News Corp stars.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian stocks end higher, News Corp stars.

text.p: SPI Futures cl 2495 +14 US 30yr cl 6.66 +0.02
10yrbond futs 92.440 -0.025 Gold NY 353.25 Lon fix 353.05
*Stocks end higher after Dow surge, metals firm. Media giant News Corp leads way after Echostar deal. Volume 409.39 million, value A$1.08 bln, 1,140 traded, 330 steady, 455 up, 355 down.
The Australian share market punched its way back above the 2,500 level to close higher on Tuesday as enthusiastic buyers came out of the woodwork.

By 4.25 p.m. (0525 GMT), the All Ordinaries index was 18.2 points higher at 2,500.8. The March share price index futures contract was 14 points higher at 2,495, a 5.8 point discount to the underlying index.

While a surge in the Dow and metals prices set the early upbeat tone, media giant News Corp led the charge in the afternoon, up over 5.5 percent to A$7.09, after it announced an alliance with EchoStar Communications Corp.
The deal with the U.S. satellite broadcaster sees News Corp take 50 percent of EchoStar and contribute assets of US$1 billion to the joint venture.

Investors gave the deal the thumbs-up and jumped into News Corp ordinary and preferred ordinary stock, with News Corp turnover by value topping A$120 million, over 10 percent of the day's total turnover.
"They certainly impressed in the afternoon but the market has been solid all day," said a Sydney broker, pointing to the active trading levels seen on the day.
"There was plenty to go around with some good volumes."
Other traders agreed, saying the market had been marching to an upbeat tempo right from the start.
"The fundamentals looked good for today's trading with the strong U.S. market and generally better commodity prices," said a Melbourne-based dealer.
Biotech group Biota saw plenty of interest, up 45 cents to A$4.55 after Monday's announcement that trials of its anti-influenza drug would start in Australia in May.
Against the trend in the resource leaders, was Woodside Petroleum, which lost 28.5 cents to A$8.745 after NYMEX crude oil futures hit their lowest level since August.

Shares in regional bank and oft-suggested takeover target, the Bank of Melbourne, were sparked by reports of comments from St George Bank that it was interested in acquisitions, despite having just merged with Advance Bank. Bank of Melbourne shares jumped 17 cents to A$8.25.
Shares in engineering, towage and hardware group Howard Smith closed up 15 cents to A$11.15 after reporting a 57 percent jump in first half net profit to A$61.34 million.
Shopping centre operator, Westfield Holdings, ended unchanged at A$19.80 after it posted a 16.6 percent jump in first half profit to A$40.93 million.
Rises outnumbered falls by a ratio of about nine to seven, while about 29 percent of stocks traded remained steady.
FUTURES/OPTIONS - Options trade boomed ahead of Thursday's February series expiry while futures trade was also active.
Total options traded 61,459 (48,096)
Turnover in March SPI contracts totalled 8,349 (4,759).

In other local markets, Australian bonds pared an initial steep price fall by the close after finding a supportive, albeit tentative, base with several hurdles locally and in the U.S. to overcome in the next few days. By 5.15 p.m. (0615 GMT), 10 year T-bonds were yielding 7.54 percent, off its early 7.60.
The Australian dollar took a small step back Tuesday as its two week upward charge finally rebounded from a stiff chart barrier at 78 cents.
By 5.15 p.m. (0615 GMT), the local dollar had sat back at US$0.7755/65 from an early US$0.7773/78 and US$0.7770/75 late here Monday.
